text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

FRANK JAMES, the brother of the more notorious JESSE, was born on this day in 1843. He was aquitted of two murders, and later retired from crime, to become a writer of "letters to the editor" of newspapers!
Australian soldier ALBERT JACKA was born in 1893. He won the first AIF VICTORIA CROSS at Gallipoli and appeared on recruiting posters for the Army.

JOHNNY RAY, the popular American singer of the 50s, was born in 1927. His stage trademark was his choking sobs. In the fifties he was considered a superstar and produced hits such as "Cry" (1951), "Just Walking In The Rain" (1956) and "Yes Tonight Josephine" (1957). He took roles in three films and had some
success with duets with DORIS DAY and FRANKIE LAINE. He died of liver failure in 1990.
American actor SAL MINEO, who sprang to fame with stars like JAMES DEAN and NATALIE WOOD, was born in 1939.
US singer, guitarist and songwriter JIM CROCE was born in 1943. He made his first recording in 1968 and had his first success with "You Don't Mess Around With Jim" (1972).
His greatest hits were "Bad Bad Leroy Brown" (1973), "Time In A Bottle" (1973) and "I'll Have To Say I Love You In A Song" (1974). He was killed in an air crash in 1973.

Rasp-voiced pop singer ROD STEWART was born in 1945. He joined the 'Faces' in 1969 after being a member of a series of groups throughout the sixties. His solo career took off in the seventies. Hits included "Maggie May" (1971), "You Wear It Well" (1972), "Sailing" (1975), "Tonight's The Night" (1976), "You're In My Heart" (1977) and "Every Beat Of My Heart" (1986).
US singer PAT BENATAR (PATRICIA ANDRZEWSKI) was born in 1952. Her hits included "Hit Me With Your Best Shot" (1980), "Love Is A Battlefield" (1983) and "We Belong" (1984).
** EVENTS **
1839 : Indian tea was auctioned for the first time in
Britain.
1840 : The PENNY POST (pre-paid post) was introduced in
Britain, ending the system under which the receiver of a letter paid for the postage.
1862 : SAMUEL COLT, firearms manufacturer who invented
the revolver that bears his name, died.
1863 : The world's first underground railway service,
London's Metropolitan line between Paddington and Farringdon, was opened.
1912 : The first flying boat, designed by GLENN CURTISS,
made its maiden flight at Hammondsport, New York.
1917 : WILLIAM FREDERICK CODY, army scout and indian
fighter known as BUFFALO BILL, died.
1920 : The League of Nations came into being.
1928 : English fliers HOOD and MONCRIEFF were lost over
the Tasman Sea attempting to fly from Australia to New Zealand.
1929 : Bushfires ravaged areas around Sydney and
Gippsland in Victoria.
1935 : MARY PICKFORD won a divorce from DOUGLAS FAIRBANKS
Senior.
1940 : Cheering crowds in Sydney farewelled the Sixth
Division, comprising 20,000 men, who were bound for the Middle East. The first convoy of Anzacs slipped out of Sydney Harbour watched by about 100,000 well-wishers.
1946 : The League Of Nations was dissolved and replaced
by the United Nations.
1949 : RCA and Columbia launched the first vinyl record
in the United States.
1957 : HAROLD MACMILLAN became Britain's new prime
minister after the resignation of Sir ANTHONY EDEN.
1969 : In the United States the 141-year-old "The
Saturday Evening Post" was published for the last time.
1975 : The Portuguese government agreed to give Angola
its independence.
1977 : CLIVE SINCLAIR introduced his 175 pound two-inch
screen.
1984 : Former Pakistani Prime Minister BENAZIR BHUTTO,
was freed from prison.
1985 : Eight people died when a gas explosion wrecked a
block of flats in the south London suburb of Putney.
1990 : China lifted martial law, imposed after the
Tiananmen Square massacre.
1996 : Israel freed hundreds of Palestinian prisoners to
jubilant relatives in the West Bank and Gaza, days before the first Palestinian national elections.
